clue.text: Burly actor mingling with group of business people

indicators.note: mingling says the letters of the two words mix together into a new order

explanation.surface: A hefty actor networks with a crowd of businessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotary Club is a service organisation whose members are local business and professional figures.

clue.text: Made a journey — not rail, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word meant is one that is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a road is a route for traffic other than the railway

explanation.surface: Someone travelled, though apparently not by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ROAD into its sound-twin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride somewhere in the past tense is to have travelled.

clue.text: Time to put in a request for something to do

parts.note: to ask is to put a request; here the word is taken as the act of asking

explanation.surface: It's time to ask for a job to keep busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put in' is only the link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or chore is a piece of work to be done.

clue.text: Book accommodation offering the best views?

explanation.surface: Booking a room with a view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is a noun, John Braine's 1957 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous English novel by John Braine, and literally a top-floor chamber with the widest outlook.

clue.text: Restaurant — artist imbibed a quantity of wine

indicators.note: imbibed means drank in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: At a bistro, a painter knocked back some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a jug of wine served at table, so it names an amount ordered.

clue.text: Promoted drudge working with pa

indicators.note: working means operating on, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A dogsbody and a personal assistant got a step up the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be raised to a higher grade or rank is to be promoted.

clue.text: Child's short note

explanation.surface: A youngster's brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is just the link 'is' between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit is an old word for a young or cheeky girl, and also a small written voucher or memo.

clue.text: It brings regulation to someone keeping watch

definitions.text: It brings regulation to someone keeping watch

parts.words: It brings regulation to someone keeping watch
parts.note: reads like a guard being disciplined, but the watch is a timepiece and the thing regulating it is the fine coil inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping watch' suggests a sentry; it is a person who owns a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine coiled balance spring governs the rate of a mechanical timepiece.

clue.text: Hector and mate fixed device giving engine speed

indicators.note: fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Hector and his friend repaired the rev counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rev counter measures how fast an engine shaft turns, in revolutions per minute.

clue.text: Put off party, you finally show anger

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word you

parts.note: to rage is to show fury

explanation.surface: Someone is deterred from a party where you lose your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to dissuade them from doing something.

clue.text: Brass component contributing to jazz in club

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The brass section adds to the jazz at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' suggests a jazz band's horns; it is the alloy of copper and this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is an alloy of copper with this metal, so it is one ingredient.

clue.text: Ms may be my baby!

parts.note: MS here is short for manuscripts, the brainchild a writer of film or stage texts might proudly claim

explanation.walkthrough: Ms looks like the title for a woman; it is the abbreviation for manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenwriter produces scripts, and the manuscripts are their creations.

clue.text: Cross fan, I can wreck hippies' meeting-place

indicators.note: wreck means smash up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An angry supporter vows to trash the flower-power gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1967 Summer of Love made this Californian city the hippie capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Its Haight-Ashbury district was the centre of the 1960s counterculture.

clue.text: Steal gift that's said to be a whatnot

indicators.note: said to be signals that the pieces only sound like the entered word

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal; a knack is a natural talent or gift

explanation.surface: A thief pockets a present described as a trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link; NICK is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot can mean a small ornament or trifle, a trinket.

clue.text: In the west, happening by chance — a new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the word's front letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: accidental means occurring by chance

explanation.surface: Out west something happens by luck, and a fresh boss takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new leader' replaces the opening A with O.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental is an adjective meaning western, of the Occident.

clue.text: Refinement shown by number when one character is replaced

indicators.note: this says a single letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: ninety is a number

explanation.surface: Polish is shown by a figure once a single letter is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The third letter, N, is replaced by C.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or subtle point of etiquette.

clue.text: Well-bred girl with endless gluttony should join gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: greed is excessive appetite

explanation.surface: A posh girl with a huge appetite ought to sign up at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'should join' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes an animal of recorded pure breeding.

clue.text: Advantage in important match about to be seized

indicators.note: to be seized means held inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a Test is a major international cricket match
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: There's an edge in a big game that's about to be grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest can mean benefit or advantage, as in acting in one's own interest.

clue.text: Greek character bends over south Americans

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
leans means tilts or bends

explanation.surface: A Greek figure stoops over the south of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only links; in an across clue the first piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a South American country, so its people are South Americans.

clue.text: Catholic comes in to make reparation without delay

indicators.note: comes in says one piece enters the other

parts.note: to atone is to make amends

explanation.surface: A Catholic arrives to make amends straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, straight away.

clue.text: Turn aside from second nasty woman

parts.note: witch is a derogatory term for an unpleasant woman

explanation.surface: Moving away from a moment with a horrible woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert or change direction is to switch.

clue.text: Fulfil promise to have an individual weapon handy?

definitions.text: to have an individual weapon handy?

explanation.surface: Honour a pledge by keeping a blade at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning re-spaces the letters as KEEP ONE'S SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Honouring a pledge is the idiom; re-spaced the letters say hold on to your blade.

clue.text: Take care of mum — in bad state after accident?

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
ma is another word for mother

explanation.surface: Look after your mother, who is in a bad way after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep unconsciousness can follow serious injury.

clue.text: Actual person who had a light named after him

definitions.text: person who had a light named after him

explanation.surface: A real man who gave his name to a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Very invented the Very light, a flare fired from a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Very can mean real or true, as in the very thing, and Edward Very gave his name to a signal flare.

clue.text: Not in favour of worker gaining independence

parts.note: a worker is a classic crossword ant
I is an abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: Opposed to an employee becoming free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed, against.

clue.text: Unhealthy condition of one member of crew after race

indicators.note: after says one piece follows the other in order

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a boat crew

explanation.surface: A rower collapses after a race in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke sets the rhythm for a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapse from overheating is a medical condition.

clue.text: Beer wanted by king Cole

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Old King Cole calls for his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cole' looks like the nursery-rhyme king; cole is a cabbage, of which kale is a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old name for brassicas such as cabbage.

clue.text: Theatre transformed in working day and prepared for anything?

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged
working means operating on, so these letters are reworked too

explanation.surface: A theatre is converted during the working day and ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' gives ATTHERE from THEATRE, 'working' gives ADY from DAY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready for immediate action is the idiom.
